title: International Scholars Award
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission (automatic consideration through the admission application)
funding_type: Partial tuition merit award (university-funded); no need-based aid for international students
administering_authority: Northeastern University — Office of Undergraduate Admissions and Student Financial Services
implementing_agency: Northeastern University — Office of Undergraduate Admissions and Student Financial Services
programme_action: Northeastern University institutional merit scholarship programme for incoming international undergraduates
description: The International Scholars Award is Northeastern University's competitive merit scholarship for incoming first-year international undergraduate students. It is awarded automatically through the application for undergraduate admission, with no separate scholarship application required. Northeastern states that awards range up to $28,000 annually and explicitly notes that the award does not cover the total cost of attendance. International students are not eligible for federal or university need-based financial aid and must demonstrate ability to fully finance their education.

award_types: International Scholars Award (competitive merit award for incoming first-year international students, awarded at admission)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: Named on the Student Financial Services international-student page as the university's merit opportunity for incoming, first-year international students. It is one of Northeastern's institutional merit awards. Other first-year merit programmes exist (Honors, Dean's, Connections, National Merit, National Recognition, Stamps, Torch, Boston/Oakland local awards) but are published for U.S. applicants and are not the international award; the Stamps Scholars Program (full cost of attendance) is separately and competitively invited and is not the International Scholars Award.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Merit scholarships are typically awarded for up to eight academic semesters provided the student: (1) maintains eligibility requirements in the individual merit scholarship contract issued with admission, which include but are not limited to a minimum GPA and/or required community service hours; (2) is enrolled full time (12 to 16 credits) and meets the enrolment requirements of their college or programme; and (3) maintains quantitative Satisfactory Academic Progress. A student who falls below the required cumulative GPA receives one probationary semester (the first in-class semester of the following academic year) in which the scholarship is still paid; if the minimum GPA is not met after that semester the scholarship is cancelled, and can only be regained by raising the GPA back to the required minimum. Awards are applied during in-class semesters when earning academic credit and are proportionally adjusted if tuition is prorated (e.g. leave of absence).
programme_structure.intake: Fall entry for first-year applicants (Boston, New York City, Oakland, London Scholars, N.U.in). Transfer and spring entry use the separate transfer process; Northeastern states limited merit scholarships are also available for transfer applicants.

status_label: Open — automatic consideration for the current first-year cycle
status_note: As of 2026-10-03 the admissions cycle for fall 2027 entry is open. Because there is no separate scholarship application, the 'deadline' is the first-year application deadline: Northeastern publishes the Regular Decision deadline of January 1 as the date by which first-year applicants are considered for merit scholarships (Early Decision I and Early Action 1 November, Early Decision II 1 January). The official pages publish month/day only, no year, so the exact calendar date for the fall 2027 cycle is not confirmed from an official page; the next cycle's consideration date is expected to be 1 January 2027. Re-verify before the November 2026 Early Decision I / Early Action round.
verification_type: Official university web pages reviewed directly on northeastern.edu subdomains (Student Financial Services, Undergraduate Admissions, Cost & Financial Aid, Deadlines & Decisions, College of Engineering)
verification_notes: Award name and value confirmed verbatim on https://studentfinance.northeastern.edu/applying-for-aid/international-students/ ('International Scholars Award — Competitive, merit-based scholarship award. Awards range up to $28,000 annually but do not cover the total cost of attendance.'). The same page confirms automatic consideration. The admissions international-applicants page states merit scholarships for international students 'range from $10,000 to $30,000 per year' and that 'No additional application is necessary, as your application for admission serves as your scholarship application.' A second, lower published range on a different official page is recorded rather than reconciled, because the university does not state which figure applies to which award year. Cost of attendance, renewal rules, deadlines, and the logo asset were each verified on separate official pages.
source_last_updated: Student Financial Services page carries a notice dated for October 2026 service hours; admissions cost page publishes 2026-2027 figures. No explicit 'last reviewed' date is published for the award itself.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Common Application / Coalition Application opens 1 August. Early Decision I: 1 November (decision by 1 January). Early Action: 1 November (decision by 15 February). Early Decision II: 1 January (decision by 1 March). Regular Decision: 1 January (decision by 1 April).
application_deadline.application_period: 2026-2027 admissions cycle, for first-year entry in fall 2027
application_deadline.official_rule: Northeastern publishes recurring month/day deadlines without a year. The governing rule for this award is that first-year applicants who apply for undergraduate admission no later than the Regular Decision deadline of January 1 are considered for merit scholarships. All first-year and transfer applicants must apply through the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Because the official pages do not attach a calendar year to 'January 1', deadline_date is left null per the accuracy rule rather than assumed to be 2027-01-01.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Do not rely on a single date from third-party listings. Northeastern's published deadlines are month/day only on the pages verified here, and the university sets separate submission dates for each application round. Missing the Regular Decision date of 1 January removes the applicant from merit scholarship consideration entirely, since the admission application is the scholarship application.

programme_duration.official_range: Bachelor's degree, typically eight academic semesters (approximately four years) of full-time study
programme_duration.renewal_note: Institutional merit scholarships are typically guaranteed for up to eight academic semesters, conditional on the merit scholarship contract terms (minimum GPA and/or community service hours), full-time enrolment (12-16 credits) and quantitative Satisfactory Academic Progress. Northeastern does not publish a single universal minimum GPA for the International Scholars Award; the figure is stated in the individual student's contract.

funding.scholarship_type: Institutional merit scholarship (partial tuition award) awarded automatically at admission
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend or allowance is published for this award. It is a tuition credit; living costs remain the student's own responsibility.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance is published. International students must separately obtain and fund health insurance that meets Massachusetts requirements; the university's student health plan is charged separately from this scholarship.
funding.institutional_costs: Applied as a tuition credit of up to $28,000 per academic year (Student Financial Services figure) / $10,000-$30,000 per year (Admissions figure). Mandatory fees, housing, food, books and personal expenses are not covered.
funding.fully_funded_note: Northeastern states explicitly that the award does not cover the total cost of attendance. Full-cost undergraduate awards at Northeastern (Stamps Scholars Program, Torch Scholars Program, Boston/Oakland local scholarships) are separate programmes and are not the International Scholars Award.

tuition.conditions: Awarded automatically at admission to admitted first-year international students; competitive. Published as 'up to' the stated ceiling, so the actual award per student may be lower. The separate admissions page publishes international merit scholarships as ranging $10,000-$30,000 per year.

visa_support.note: Not published in official source. International admitted students separately request a Form I-20 or DS-2019 through the Office of Global Services.

insurance.note: Not published in official source. Massachusetts law requires students to participate in a qualifying health plan; Northeastern's Student Health Plan is billed separately and is not part of this scholarship.

book_allowance.note: Not published in official source. Books and course materials are an estimated indirect cost of about $1,000 for 2026-2027.

accommodation_support.note: Not published in official source. Housing is estimated separately at $13,612 for 2026-2027 and first-year students are required to live on campus for their first two years.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published. Recipients do sign a merit scholarship contract as part of the financial aid offer, and outside awards, not this scholarship, can reduce institutional aid.

total_estimated_value.note: Not published as a single total. A tuition credit of up to $28,000 per academic year for up to eight semesters is the ceiling, not a guaranteed four-year total, and no 'total value' figure is published by the university.

coverage: Partial tuition credit, published as up to $28,000 per academic year (Student Financial Services, International Students page)
Merit award for international students published as ranging from $10,000 to $30,000 per year (Undergraduate Admissions, International Applicants page)
Renewable for up to eight academic semesters subject to contract terms
Awarded automatically through the admission application, with no separate scholarship application
coverage_limitations: The award does not cover the total cost of attendance; Northeastern states this explicitly.
International students are not eligible for federal or university-provided need-based financial aid, so this merit award is the only institutional aid route for international first-year applicants.
Mandatory fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation are not covered.
The amount is individual and competitive; the published figures are ceilings/ranges, not a guaranteed amount for any applicant.

Benefits are conditioned on full-time enrolment and the stated academic performance in the individual merit scholarship contract; a fall below the required cumulative GPA that is not corrected after one probationary semester cancels the scholarship.
Exact benefit structure and renewal GPA may differ per student and may change with Board of Trustees revision of tuition and fees.

Two different official pages publish different value ranges for international merit scholarships ($10,000-$30,000 vs up to $28,000); Northeastern does not reconcile them, so neither should be treated as exact.
eligible_applicants: Incoming first-year international applicants (non-U.S. citizens) applying to Northeastern from a high school in any country, including from inside the United States
U.S. citizens applying to Northeastern from a high school outside the United States, who are reviewed under the same international-applicant process

Applicants across all of Northeastern's undergraduate colleges and programs, including the College of Engineering (which directs applicants to the central admissions and financial aid pages rather than running a separate international merit scholarship)
Applicants admitted through Northeastern's enrollment opportunities (Boston, New York City, Oakland, London Scholars, N.U.in)
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the bachelor's-completion sense. This award funds entry INTO a bachelor's degree. Applicants must be completing a pre-university education programme and must earn a graduation certificate or diploma that qualifies them to apply to university in their home country before enrolling; final official transcripts and final national examination results are required by 30 June for the entering class.
equivalent_degree_note: Northeastern accepts a wide range of pre-university qualifications in place of a U.S. high school diploma, including the High School Diploma, IB Diploma, GCE A-Levels, French Baccalauréat, Bachillerato, German Abitur, Swiss Maturität/Maturité/Maturità, Attestat o Srednem (Polnom) Obshchem Obrazovanii, Indian Standard XII Higher Secondary School Certificate, CAPE, HKDSE, Malaysian STPM and WASSCE. Up to 32 advanced credits may be awarded for AP, IB, GCE A-Level, French Baccalauréat, German Abitur or Swiss Maturität results.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published for this award or for first-year admission on the official Northeastern pages read: https://admissions.northeastern.edu/application-information/international-applicants-2/ and https://studentfinance.northeastern.edu/applying-for-aid/international-students/

eligibility.citizenship: Open to international (non-U.S. citizen) applicants worldwide, and to U.S. citizens applying from a high school outside the United States. No country quota or nationality cap is published.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must be applying from a high school in any country, including the United States. No minimum residence period in a given country is published.
eligibility.age_limit: No age minimum or maximum is published on the official pages reviewed.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion of a pre-university education programme earning a graduation certificate or diploma that enables application to university in the applicant's home country (High School Diploma, IB Diploma, A-Levels, Baccalauréat, and equivalents). A final official transcript and, where applicable, final national examination results must be submitted by 30 June.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Holistic and competitive; no published GPA cut-off, class-rank or score threshold for this award. Northeastern is test-optional, states applicants are not penalised for applying without SAT/ACT, and states that no part of the application may be completed by paid agents or admissions consultancies.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: HOLISTIC — no minimum GPA is published for admission or for this award. A separate, different figure exists only for transfer applicants ('Our most competitive candidates for transfer admission typically have a grade-point average of 3.500 or higher'), which is an admissions statement for transfers and is NOT a threshold for this first-year award. The renewal GPA is stated in each student's individual merit scholarship contract and is not published.
eligibility.language_requirement: Non-native English-speaking applicants must submit official results from an approved English language test (Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency, Duolingo English Test, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, or TOEFL Internet-based Test including the Home Edition) or request a waiver. Results must be no more than two years old at the application deadline. Northeastern will not accept IELTS Indicator, TOEFL Essentials or TOEFL ITP Plus for China. Applicants may alternatively be considered for NU Immerse, a one-year transitional English and acculturation programme.
eligibility.work_experience: No work experience requirement is published for this award.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: No formal extracurricular requirement is published; Northeastern reviews applications holistically and separately runs invitation-only programmes (University Honors Program, Stamps Scholars) with their own processes.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: No published leadership requirement for this award.
eligibility.financial_need: Need is NOT a criterion. The award is merit-based. However, admission is need-aware for international students, meaning ability to cover educational costs is considered in the admissions decision.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Northeastern National Scholarships replace other institutional merit awards (Honors, Dean's, Connections, Sophomore Achievement, International Scholars and similar) and may change previously awarded Northeastern University Grant funds; a student designated as both a National Recognition Scholar and a National Merit Finalist is eligible for only one National Scholarship. National Merit Semifinalists or National Recognition Program Scholars in the London double-degree programme are not eligible for the National Scholarship.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time enrolment (12 to 16 credits) is required to maintain the award, with the award applied only during in-class semesters when the student is earning academic credit.
eligibility.health_requirement: A Health Report Form with medical consent and immunization records must be returned to University Health and Counseling Services by the end of June for enrolling students. Massachusetts law requires participation in a qualifying student health insurance plan.
eligibility.field_restrictions: No field-of-study or major restriction is published. The College of Engineering directs applicants to the central admissions and financial aid pages and runs no separate entering-student international scholarship.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage, GPA or score threshold is published for the International Scholars Award. Northeastern is test-optional and states applicants who apply without standardized testing 'will not be penalized or disadvantaged'.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: No separate scholarship-specific academic requirement. Admission requirements apply: a completed pre-university programme, official high school transcript sent directly by the school, a Secondary School Report, recommendation letters, optional standardized testing, English proficiency for non-native speakers, and the Declaration and Certification of Finances. Engineering applicants must have taken physics, chemistry and precalculus, with at least four years of English, two years of history, two years of one foreign language, three years of science and three years of mathematics.
selection_factors_may_include: Strength and trend of the secondary school academic record
Rigour of the completed curriculum, including IB/A-Levels/AP and advanced coursework
Predicted or final results in national examinations (highly recommended for overseas national-exam systems)
Optional standardized testing (SAT or ACT) if the applicant chooses to submit it
Coherence with Northeastern's experiential and global learning model
Optional third-party unscripted video interviews (InitialView or Vericant), which do not replace English testing
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Northeastern evaluates complete applications holistically. It publishes no rubric, weighting or score cut-off for the International Scholars Award, and states that all complete applications are 'fully considered for admission to Northeastern, invitation to the University Honors Program, and any merit scholarships'.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Northeastern will waive the English proficiency requirement for applicants who complete four consecutive academic years in a high school or university where native English was the primary instructional language for all courses (except foreign language courses) AND who also meet one of the stated exceptions (achievement of 4 or 5 on AP English Language & Composition; 5 or higher on IB English A: Language & Literature or Literature (HL/SL), 6 or 7 on HL English B, or 7 on SL English B; B or higher on GCE A-Level or AS-Level English Language or Literature; B/6 or higher on GCSE or IGCSE English Language or Literature; B or higher on GCE O-Level English Language; or, for the American or British Option Internationale du Baccalauréat, 12 or higher on English Language & Literature). Applicants whose schools did not offer AP/IB/A-Levels may request a waiver if they completed secondary education in a majority native-English-speaking country with no grade lower than a B in any English language, literature or composition course.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The scores Northeastern publishes are NOT cut-off or minimum scores. The official page states the published ranges 'represent the middle 50% score ranges for students who were admitted and enrolled as first-year students in Fall 2020 and Spring 2021' and that they are 'not cut-off scores, but for estimating purposes, and in no way represent a promise or guarantee of admission'. Published middle-50% ranges: Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185-204; Duolingo English Test 120-130; IELTS Academic 7.0-8.0; PTE Academic 68-76; TOEFL iBT 99-108. Therefore every 'minimum_*' field is null by design. Results must be sent directly from the testing agency, must be no more than two years old at the application deadline, and are focused on the most recent result; Northeastern does not superscore English tests and does not consider TOEFL MyBest scores.
accepted_tests: TOEFL Internet-Based Test (iBT), including the TOEFL iBT Home Edition

language_of_instruction.language_note: All Northeastern bachelor's programmes are taught in English. A one-year transitional English and academic preparation route (NU Immerse) exists for students whose test results indicate a need for additional English support but who otherwise meet the academic requirements of the degree programme applied to.

application_method.application_route: Apply through the Common Application or the Coalition Application directly to the Northeastern University Office of Undergraduate Admissions. There is no separate scholarship application and no central or third-party scholarship portal.
application_steps: Submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, including Northeastern-specific questions and essays, by the relevant first-year deadline (1 November for Early Decision I or Early Action; 1 January for Early Decision II or Regular Decision).

Request that your high school send official transcripts and academic records directly to Northeastern by the application deadline; transcripts sent by the student, family or an independent consultant are not accepted.
Submit the Secondary School Report (or College Report for transfer applicants), counselor recommendation and required recommendation letters.

Optionally submit SAT or ACT scores (Northeastern is test-optional and superscores only across the two test types). Non-native English speakers must submit an approved English test result or request a waiver.
Optionally submit a third-party unscripted video interview through InitialView or Vericant by the round deadline (ED I 15 November; EA 1 December; ED II 15 January; RD 1 February).
Complete and submit the Declaration and Certification of Finances (DCF) through your Application Status Check to document financial support for at least one academic year.
Complete the Coursework and Grades Form through your Application Status Check when it becomes available.

Complete the enrollment deposit and one-time International Student Fee by 1 May (for Early Action / Regular Decision admits), then apply for housing and request the I-20 or DS-2019 through the Office of Global Services.
If admitted, review the Offer of Financial Assistance in your Application Status Check, which lists the merit scholarship, its terms, and any contract of understanding to sign.

official_application_documents.document_language: Documents must be in English. Official English translations are required for documents provided in another language, issued by a school official or a translation agency accredited in the country of the educational institution.
official_application_documents.document_format: Documents are submitted online through the Common Application or Coalition Application; documents not submitted through the application can be sent from a verifiable high school or university email address to admissions@northeastern.edu or mailed to the Office of Undergraduate Admissions (200 Kerr Hall, 360 Huntington Ave, Boston, MA 02115-5000) or to Northeastern University Application Processing Center, P.O. Box 8210, Portsmouth, NH 03802 USA.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Official transcript required, sent directly by the high school or university. Transcripts sent by the applicant, their family or an independent educational consultant will not be accepted. Final official transcripts are required before enrolment, and international transfer applicants seeking transfer credit after admission must provide a certified course-by-course credential evaluation from a recognised agency (CED, SpanTran, WES or similar).
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Yes — certified/official English translations are required for documents in any other language, issued by a school official or an accredited translation agency.

selection_process.decision_maker: Northeastern University Office of Undergraduate Admissions, in coordination with Student Financial Services for the financial aid package
selection_process.selection_type: Automatic consideration within a holistic, competitive admissions review; no separate scholarship application, interview or committee stage is published for this award
possible_stages: Application completeness review (including transcripts, reports, recommendations, English proficiency and DCF)
Holistic academic and personal review by the Admissions Committee
Merit scholarship consideration at the time of admission for all first-year applicants who apply by the Regular Decision deadline
Financial aid packaging and release with the offer of admission (Regular Decision notifies by 1 April)
Merit scholarship contract issued with the financial aid offer, which the student signs
selection_process.weighting_note: Northeastern publishes no rubric, weighting, score cut-off or minimum GPA for the International Scholars Award. The university states only that merit scholarships are 'extremely competitive'. Any weighting would therefore be invented, so none is recorded.
selection_process.results_timing: Merit scholarship awards are notified at the time of admission, in the Offer of Financial Assistance released through the Application Status Check. Published notification dates: Early Decision I by 1 January, Early Action by 15 February, Early Decision II by 1 March, Regular Decision by 1 April. Separate invitation-only processes (for example Stamps Scholars, with a video application) notify nominees and alternates in mid-March.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Northeastern does not publish the number of International Scholars Awards conferred, the award distribution, or any rank ordering of recipients.

selection_criteria.academic_excellence: Primary published basis for merit scholarships ('reward outstanding academic achievement'), reviewed holistically with no published threshold
selection_criteria.leadership: Not published as a criterion for this award
selection_criteria.community_service: Not published as a selection criterion, but service hours may appear as a renewal condition in the individual merit scholarship contract
selection_criteria.extracurricular_achievement: Considered as part of the holistic application review; not published as a separate criterion for this award
selection_criteria.financial_need: Not a criterion. Admission for international students is need-aware, meaning ability to cover educational costs is considered in the admissions decision
selection_criteria.additional_factors: Fit with Northeastern's experiential, global learning model; rigour of curriculum; predicted or final national examination results; strength of Northeastern-specific application responses; optional standardized testing; optional third-party unscripted interview

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from the selected Northeastern undergraduate college, across more than 175 undergraduate majors
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Eight academic semesters (approximately four years) of full-time study
possible_awards: Bachelor of Science in a named engineering discipline
degree_outcome.degree_note: The International Scholars Award funds one of Northeastern's undergraduate degrees. First-year students enter a college rather than a restricted major in most cases, and Northeastern's cooperative education programme is part of the undergraduate experience. Advanced credit of up to 32 credits may be granted for AP, IB, GCE A-Level, French Baccalauréat, German Abitur or Swiss Maturität results.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Up to 32 advanced credits may be awarded for AP, IB, GCE A-Level, French Baccalauréat, German Abitur or Swiss Maturität examinations. Credit is generally awarded for IB Higher Level scores of 5, 6 or 7, and for AP scores of 4 or greater in engineering programmes; advanced credit is not granted until the original or official certificate is received and evaluated. International transfer applicants may need a certified course-by-course credential evaluation.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: The award is applied as a tuition credit of up to $28,000 per academic year. All tuition and fees are subject to revision by the Board of Trustees. Northeastern's published 2026-2027 first-year cost of attendance for the Boston, New York City and Oakland campuses is $98,322 (tuition $71,050; fees $1,650; housing $13,612; food $9,210; books and course materials $1,000; personal expenses $900; transportation $900).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No waiver of the USD 75 application fee is published for scholarship recipients; fee waiver requests are handled through an application question in the application itself.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients are issued a merit scholarship contract with the financial aid offer — Northeastern states that 'Eligibility requirements include, but are not limited to, a minimum GPA and/or required community service hours' and that many scholarships require signing a contract of understanding. Separately, all enrolling students complete a Student Financial Responsibility Agreement through the Student Hub before orientation.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Office of Global Services (I-20/DS-2019 issuance, SEVIS compliance, employment and OPT guidance); University Health and Counseling Services; mandatory International Student Check-In and Clearance Session; international student orientation; academic advising; on-campus employment with proper authorisation; monthly payment plans via Flywire; supplemental private loans for international students with a creditworthy U.S. co-signer.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No service bond or repayment obligation is published for this award. Failure to maintain the renewal conditions cancels the scholarship prospectively; it is not converted into a debt. Students with a past-due balance over 90 days may be referred to a collection agency, which is a general billing policy rather than a scholarship condition.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will complete a pre-university education programme that qualifies you to apply to university in your home country
Have your school send the official transcript directly (do not send it yourself)
Secure predicted grades for your national examination system — strongly recommended and often decisive
Book an approved English test early, or assess whether you qualify for a waiver
Prepare the Declaration and Certification of Finances showing at least one full academic year of funding
Budget for the gap: even a maximum $28,000 award leaves roughly $70,000 per year of the $98,322 published cost of attendance
Plan for the $600 enrollment deposit plus one-time International Student Fee by 1 May
Draft essays that respond to the Northeastern-specific questions rather than reusing generic essays
Consider an optional InitialView or Vericant interview, but never as a substitute for English testing
Do not use a paid agent or admissions consultancy — Northeastern will reject materials and revoke offers
programme_comparison_fields: Whether the award can ever reach full cost of attendance (this one cannot)
Need-based aid availability (none for international students at Northeastern)
Whether the university is need-aware for international applicants (Northeastern is)
Whether the award is restricted to a particular campus or enrolment opportunity
Round of application (the same award is available in ED I, EA, ED II and RD)
Whether a local/campus-restricted full-cost award (Boston/Oakland) exists separately
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The Northeastern-specific questions are the main place to demonstrate fit. Focus on concrete, verifiable accomplishments and what the applicant would do with Northeastern's experiential, global model rather than generic ambition. Northeastern requires the application to be completed entirely by the applicant, so the writing must be the student's own and consistent with the academic record and predicted grades.
profile_fit_labels: Strong academic record from an overseas national examination system
Applicant who can fund roughly $70,000+ per year of remaining costs
Applicant who wants a U.S. co-op/internship-heavy undergraduate experience
Applicant applying to a U.S. research university without expecting a full ride
Engineering or computer science applicant (no separate COE award; central merit applies)
Applicant who will complete the DCF with documented family or sponsor funding

Believing a separate scholarship application is required — the admission application IS the scholarship application
Submitting transcripts through the applicant, family or an independent consultant, which Northeastern will not accept
Treating the published English score ranges as minimum cut-offs; they are middle-50% enrolment ranges from Fall 2020/Spring 2021
Missing the 1 January Regular Decision date, which removes the applicant from merit consideration entirely

risk_flags.risk: Merit award is far below the total cost of attendance
risk_flags.impact: A maximum $28,000 award against a published $98,322 annual cost leaves roughly $70,000 to be funded from family, sponsors, private loans or outside scholarships
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget for the full gap from the outset; aggressively pursue outside scholarships, and confirm the DCF documents the full one-year amount even if the applicant expects more aid later

risk_flags.risk: No need-based financial aid for international students
risk_flags.impact: A financially strong applicant without a large merit award has no institutional fallback, and undergraduate admission is need-aware for international students
risk_flags.mitigation: Only apply if the family can evidence a full academic year of funding; do not rely on a future appeal, since Northeastern does not publish a need-based appeal route for international undergraduates

risk_flags.risk: Two conflicting official value ranges ($10,000-$30,000 per year vs up to $28,000)
risk_flags.impact: Applicants may budget against the wrong ceiling and overestimate the likely award
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat both figures as published ranges rather than commitments and verify the actual amount in the Offer of Financial Assistance before committing to the deposit

risk_flags.risk: Deadline published as month/day only, with no calendar year
risk_flags.impact: A database or aggregator that converts 'January 1' into a single dated deadline may drift from the actual cycle date
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-verify the cycle dates before each November and January round; this record deliberately leaves deadline_date null rather than inventing a year

risk_flags.risk: Renewal depends on an unpublished, contract-specific minimum GPA
risk_flags.impact: A student cannot know the exact GPA they must hold until the contract arrives, and a single fall below it puts the award at risk after one probationary semester
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the merit scholarship contract at admission and raise any ambiguity with Student Financial Services immediately; consider requesting the minimum GPA in writing before enrolling

risk_flags.risk: Out-of-date fee and tuition data across official pages
risk_flags.impact: Figures such as the International Student Fee appear as different amounts on different official pages, and tuition is revised annually by the Board of Trustees
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-check the Student Financial Services tuition and fees page and the admissions cost page each cycle; treat every figure as year-specific

risk_flags.risk: Missing the 30 June final transcript and examination results
risk_flags.impact: Northeastern reserves the right to rescind an offer of admission if final results are outside an acceptable range of predicted results, which would end the scholarship with it
risk_flags.mitigation: Ensure exam boards and schools send final results promptly, and use the extension route if the school's calendar differs rather than waiting

risk_flags.impact: Any part of the application completed by a paid agent or consultancy leads to rejection of materials, revocation of an admissions offer, cancellation of admission or involuntary withdrawal
risk_flags.mitigation: Complete every field personally and keep evidence of authorship; avoid admissions consultancies that promise to write any part of the application

database_notes: Official award name confirmed as 'International Scholars Award'. The research brief's informal labels ('Northeastern International Student Scholarship', 'Global Scholars') do not appear on any official Northeastern page read, so legacy_titles is empty rather than populated with invented names.
short_title 'ISA' is a derived abbreviation of the official name, not an acronym used by Northeastern. No official short form is published.

The College of Engineering (coe.northeastern.edu) publishes no separate international merit scholarship for entering undergraduates; its Undergraduate Admissions & Aid page directs applicants to the central admissions site, so the College of Engineering is covered by the same institutional award recorded here.

A genuine conflict exists between two official pages on the award's value: Student Financial Services states awards range 'up to $28,000 annually', while Undergraduate Admissions states merit scholarships for international students 'range from $10,000 to $30,000 per year'. Both are recorded verbatim and neither is reconciled or selected as authoritative.

Deadline_date is null by design. Northeastern publishes its first-year deadlines as month/day (1 November and 1 January) without a calendar year on every page read, so converting them to a dated deadline for fall 2027 entry would be an invention. The record states the expected cycle date only as an expectation.

Northeastern's published English test figures are explicitly middle-50% ranges for students admitted and enrolled in Fall 2020 and Spring 2021, not cut-offs. Every minimum_* field is therefore null. Recording any of these numbers as a minimum would misrepresent the official source.
The renewal minimum GPA is not published anywhere; Northeastern states it is set in each student's individual merit scholarship contract. No figure is recorded.
No published age limit, gender restriction or nationality quota was found, so those fields are null/false rather than inferred.

The one-time International Student Fee is published as $450 on the Student Financial Services tuition and fees schedule (verified by direct extraction) but the admissions enrollment-deposit section refers to a one-time International Student Fee of $350. The $450 figure from the financial authority's fee schedule is used, and the discrepancy is flagged for verification.

The $98,322 cost of attendance and its line items are Northeastern's 2026-2027 estimates for the Boston, New York City and Oakland campuses and are explicitly 'subject to Board of Trustee approval'. Note also that the university's own net price calculators state they are 'not intended for international, transfer, returning, graduate, or College of Professional Studies students'.

Northeastern's ISCED level is not stated on any official page read. 'ISCED Level 6 equivalent' is a standard mapping of a U.S. bachelor's degree and is noted here as an interpretation rather than a published fact.

The 'Dean's Scholarship' figure of up to $28,000 mentioned on some search-engine snippets could not be verified: the Student Financial Services first-year scholarships URL now returns HTTP 404, so that award is not recorded here.
